Voynich MS - Quire 2

General

For an explanation of the material found on this page, see here.

Description

Quire 2 is a standard quire containing folios 9 through 16. The gathering mark is on f16v. Folio 12 is missing.

Schematic folio layout:

Folio 9

Normal folio. The folio nr. is on f9r.

f9r  

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.
It has the folio nr (9) in the upper right corner.

Illustration(s)

Plant with weird leaves, earth plateau and peculiar (hairy) roots. No flowers but some kind of seeds.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
α: stem-root line
α: stalk connects to leaf centre
α: flat-topped root

Text

This page has 10 text items (loci), as follows:
10 lines of standard text in paragraphs, of which one is centred.

The text is in two paragraphs. They are interrupted by the plant drawing. The last line of the second paragraph is centred.

Currier language: A
RZ language: A (page) / A (folio) / A (bifolio)
LFD hand: 1

Browse interlinear transliteration of f9r

Tentative identifications

ELV: delphinium? ThP: chalidonium magna.

Other information

 

  f9v

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.

Illustration(s)

Plant with plain roots, two types of leaves and characteristic flowers.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
α: veined leaves
α: two distinct leaf shapes

Text

This page has 12 text items (loci), as follows:
12 lines of standard text in paragraphs;

The text is in two paragraphs. The text carefully avoids the drawings.

There are several individual characters written in or near the flowers, using the Latin alphabet. In the top left flower under the blue paint: 'por' (tentative) in the top petal, 'p' in the bottom left petal and barely legible ('r'?) in the bottom right petal; an unclear letter or scribble just right of the top petal.

There is a clear single 'g' just right of the top right flower.

Currier language: A
RZ language: A (page) / A (folio) / A (bifolio)
LFD hand: 1

Browse interlinear transliteration of f9v

Tentative identifications

This is one of the most recognisable plants in the MS, and seems to represent some type of pansy or 'viola'. Even the colours are realistic. The individual flowers have been drawn 'upside down'.

ELV: viola, pansy. ThP: viola tricoloris, herba trinitatis (O'Neill)

Other information

The characters in or near the flowers appear like colour annotations (for which see here).
